Make we are using a sufficient default block size. Ref https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/49514

### What changed and how does it work?

issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
the issue happened in two cases, one 2TB data, another 12TB data, both are using v8.1.2 version. current guess of the root cause is that pebble might have some bug, causes memory usage burst, and OOM, as the time window is very short, and pebble might allocate memory using CGO, we hasn't got any useful heap profile.
and we found that in v8.1.1 we have upgrade pebble to v1.1 in https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/commit/888a58b0064b060a136332c583e08ac2a6199fd4 since v8.1.1. so we try import the same data using v7.5.5, and it success.

we found a pebble OOM issue https://github.com/cockroachdb/pebble/issues/3039, it might related

so the trigger condition might include
- import large data set, say 2T. (we have tested with smaller data-set, say several hundreds of GB, no such issue)
- using version >= v8.1.1 which have upgraded pebble

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
success
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
oom on ingest
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
v8.1.2
<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
comments:
/type regression
Mark this one as regression since the same operation succeeded on an earlier version.

After extensive reproduction and debugging, the root cause of this issue is multifaceted:

1. PR Impact ([#49514](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/49514)):

- When making BlockSize configurable, the PR did not ensure that the default value remained consistent with the previous version (16KB) when no parameter was provided.
- As a result, the engine defaulted to Pebble’s native 4KB block size, significantly increasing the meta size of SST files.
- Under high-concurrency workloads, this led to a sharp rise in peak memory usage, ultimately triggering OOM.

2. Cache Configuration Optimization:

- Pebble was initialized without an explicit Cache option, causing it to default to an 8MB Cache (4 shards, each 2MB).
- With large SST files, the index meta could not fit into the Cache, forcing each worker to maintain its own index entries, further increasing peak memory usage.
- This highlights a key area for further optimization—ensuring proper Cache configuration to mitigate excessive memory overhead.
